algorithms.name: E2D with inverse gap weighting and Vovk-Azoury-Warmuth regression (SquareCB-style)
E2D with PC-IGW (Policy Cover Inverse Gap Weighting)

bound.regime: any gamma_dec > sqrt(C_T*T) (bound is max over such gamma)

symbols.dec_low: localized DEC sup_{Mbar in M} dec_gamma(M_{eps}(Mbar),Mbar) with eps = gamma/(C_T T)
symbols.C_T: 2^15 log(2T ∧ V(M)), V(M) a density-ratio bound

conditions: holds with probability at least delta/2 for some model in M

source.label: thm:lower_main
source.quote: Consider a model class $\cM$ with $\cF_{\cM}\subseteq(\Act\to\brk*{0,1})$, and let $\delta\in(0,1)$ and $T\in\bbN$ be fixed. Define $\Ct\ldef{}2^{15}\log(2T\wedge{}\abscont)$ ... Then for any algorithm, there exists a model in $\cM$ for which $\RegDM\geq{}(6\Ct)^{-1}\cdot\max_{\gamma>\sqrt{\Ct{}T}}\min\crl[\Big]{\prn*{\compthmone-15\delta}\cdot{}T,\;\gamma}$ with probability at least $\delta/2$.

results.notes: Bound holds with moderate probability delta/2, so recorded as realized_regret/high_probability. Max over gamma rendered as a free gamma.

symbols.dec_inf: max_gamma sup_{Mbar} dec_gamma(M^inf_{eps}(Mbar),Mbar), L_inf-localized DEC with eps = gamma/(C_T T), C_T = 2^11 log(2T ∧ V(M))

source.label: thm:lower_main_expectation
source.quote: Consider a model class $\cM$ with $\cF_{\cM}\subseteq(\Act\to\brk*{0,1})$. Let $T\in\bbN$ be fixed and define $\Ct\ldef{}2^{11}\log(2T\wedge{}\abscont)$ ... Then for any algorithm, there exists a model in $\cM$ for which $\En\brk*{\RegDM}\geq{}6^{-1}\cdot\max_{\gamma>0}\sup_{\Mbar\in\cM}\comp(\cMinf[\vepslowg](\Mbar),\Mbar)\cdot{}T.$

results.notes: Regret defined via mean rewards -> pseudo_regret.

bound.regime: any gamma_dec > 0 (bound is min over gamma)

symbols.dec_up: sup_{Mbar in co(M)} dec_gamma(M_{eps}(Mbar),Mbar) with eps = 48(gamma/T log(|M|/delta) + sup dec(M,Mbar) + 1/gamma)
symbols.M_size: |M|, size of the finite model class

tuning: Option II with appropriate gamma, confidence radius and estimation oracle

source.label: thm:upper_main
source.quote: Fix $\delta\in(0,1)$. Assume that $\Rspace\subseteq\brk*{0,1}$ and \pref{ass:localization_constant} holds. Define $C=\bigoh(\Cloc^{2}\log_{\Cloc}(T))$ ... Then \pref{alg:main}, with an appropriate choice for parameters and estimation oracle, ensures that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\RegDM \leq{} C\cdot{}\min_{\gamma>0}\max\crl[\bigg]{\sup_{\Mbar\in\conv(\cM)}\comp(\cMloc[\vepsupg](\Mbar),\Mbar)\cdot{}T,\; \gamma\cdot{}\log(\abs{\cM}/\delta)}.$

results.notes: Computational efficiency depends on solving the DEC minimax program; not stated generally.

symbols.B_dens: density bound B of Assumption ass:finite_measure
symbols.est_M: model estimation complexity inf_eps {log N(M,eps) + eps^2 T}
symbols.dec_up: localized DEC over co(M) with radius C_2(gamma/T (est_M + log(1/delta)) + sup dec + 1/gamma)

source.label: thm:upper_main_infinite
source.quote: Assume that $\Rspace\subseteq\brk*{0,1}$ and that \pref{ass:finite_measure} holds. Define $C_1=\bigoh(\Cloc^2\log_{\Cloc}(T)\log^2(BT))$ ... guarantees that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\RegDM \leq{} C_1\cdot{}\min_{\gamma>0}\max\crl[\bigg]{\sup_{\Mbar\in\conv(\cM)}\comp(\cMloc[\vepsupg](\Mbar),\Mbar)\cdot{}T,\; \gamma\cdot{}(\MComp +\log(\delta^{-1}))}.$

results.notes: General (covering-number) version of thm:upper_main.

symbols.est_Pi: decision-space estimation complexity inf_eps {log N(Pi_M,eps) + eps T}

conditions: conclusion of Proposition prop:minimax_swap holds (e.g. finite decision space, bounded rewards, countable supports)

source.label: thm:upper_main_bayes
source.quote: Whenever the conclusion of \pref{prop:minimax_swap} holds, there exists an algorithm that ensures that $\En\brk*{\RegDM} \leq{} 2\cdot\min_{\gamma>0}\max\crl*{\comp(\conv(\cM))\cdot{}T,\;\; \inf_{\veps\geq{}0}\crl*{\gamma\cdot\log\ActCov +\veps\cdot{}T}} \leq{} 2\cdot\min_{\gamma>0}\max\crl*{\comp(\conv(\cM))\cdot{}T,\; (1+\gamma)\cdot{}\ActComp}.

results.notes: Non-constructive (minimax swap). For finite Pi_M, also 2 min_gamma max{dec(co M) T, gamma log|Pi_M|}.

symbols.dec_hat: sup over estimator range of dec_gamma(M,Mbar)
symbols.Est_H: cumulative Hellinger estimation error of the oracle

source.label: thm:upper_general
source.quote: \pref{alg:main} with \optionone and exploration parameter $\gamma>0$ guarantees that $\RegDM \leq{} \sup_{\Mbar\in\cMhat}\comp(\cM,\Mbar)\cdot{}T + \gamma\cdot\EstHel$ almost surely.

results.notes: Regret here is the random sum of conditional expected gaps; holds almost surely. Theorem also gives a high-probability version with Est_H(T,delta) and a localized Option II bound (not recorded separately).

symbols.dec_dual_co: sup_{Mbar in co(M)} dual (Bayesian) DEC of co(M)

source.label: prop:bayes_basic
source.quote: For parameter $\gamma>0$, \pref{alg:bayes_basic} guarantees that $\En_{\Mstar\sim\mu}\En\sups{\Mstar}\brk*{\RegDM} \leq{} \sup_{\Mbar\in\conv(\cM)}\compb(\conv(\cM),\Mbar)\cdot{}T +\gamma\cdot\log\abs{\Pim}.$

symbols.dec_ctx: sup over contexts x of the D-DEC of the projected class M|_x relative to estimator range
symbols.Est_D: cumulative estimation error of the oracle w.r.t. divergence D on the observed contexts

source.label: thm:upper_contextual
source.quote: \pref{alg:contextual} with exploration parameter $\gamma>0$ guarantees that $\RegCDM \leq{} \sup_{x\in\cX}\compgen(\cMx,\cMhatx)\cdot{}T + \gamma\cdot\EstCD$ almost surely.

results.notes: Applications in text: finite actions O(sqrt(AT Est_Sq)) (SquareCB), linear O~(sqrt(dT Est_Sq)), tabular contextual RL O(sqrt(H^3 SAT Est_Sq)).

source.label: eq:posterior_mab
source.number: Section 5.1 (Regret upper bound paragraph, via Theorem thm:upper_main_bayes and Proposition prop:posterior_mab)
source.quote: By plugging the bound on the \CompText from \pref{prop:posterior_mab} into \pref{thm:upper_main_bayes} ..., we conclude existence of an algorithm with $\En\brk*{\RegDM} \leq{} 2\cdot\min_{\gamma>0}\max\crl*{\frac{AT}{\gamma}, \gamma\log{}A} = 4\sqrt{AT\log{}A}.$

results.notes: Derived in text, not a formal statement. Constant 4 as stated by paper (the min-max computes to 2 sqrt(AT log A)). Existence via minimax theorem; E2D.Bayes is explicit only for the Bayesian setting.

source.number: Section 5.1.2 (Regret upper bound paragraph, via Proposition prop:igw_mab and Theorem thm:upper_general_distance)
source.quote: we can estimate the rewards using the Vovk-Azoury-Warmuth algorithm ..., which has $\En\brk{\EstSq}\leq{}A\log(T)$. The resulting algorithm has $\En\brk*{\RegDM}\leq{}A\sqrt{T\log(T)}$, and runs in time $\bigoh(A)$ per round.

results.notes: Text derivation; constant appears informal. Follows Foster & Rakhlin (2020) approach.

source.label: prop:mab_lower
source.number: Section 5.1.3 (Regret lower bound paragraph, via Proposition prop:mab_lower and Theorem thm:lower_main_expectation)
source.quote: If we choose $\gamma=C\cdot\sqrt{AT}$ for $C>0$ sufficiently large, we have that $\En\brk*{\RegDM} \geq{} \Omega(\sqrt{AT})$, which matches the minimax rate for the problem

results.notes: Recovers known minimax lower bound via the DEC. DEC bound itself: dec >= 2^-6 A/gamma.

source.label: prop:bandit_upper_linear
source.quote: Combining this strategy with \pref{thm:upper_main_bayes}, we obtain $\En\brk{\RegDM}\leq{}\bigoh(\sqrt{dT\log\abs{\Act}})$ when $\abs{\Act}<\infty$

results.notes: Text consequence; K here denotes number of actions |Pi|.

conditions: Theta and Pi have bounded diameter

source.label: prop:bandit_upper_linear
source.quote: for infinite action spaces we obtain $\En\brk{\RegDM}\leq\bigoht(d\sqrt{T})$ whenever $\Theta$ and $\Act$ have bounded diameter; both results are optimal.

results.notes: Text consequence.

source.label: prop:bandit_lower_linear
source.quote: Combining this result with \pref{thm:lower_main_expectation} leads to a lower bound of the form $\En\brk*{\RegDM}\geq\bigom(\sqrt{dT})$.

results.notes: Not tight (optimal is d sqrt T). DEC bound: dec >= d/(12 gamma) for gamma >= 2d/3.

conditions: reward functions concave and 1-Lipschitz with values in [0,1]

source.label: prop:bandit_upper_convex
source.quote: Since this setting has $\ActComp\leq\bigoht(d)$ whenever $\diam(\Act)=\bigoh(1)$, combining the bound above with \pref{thm:upper_main_bayes} leads to regret $\En\brk{\RegDM}\leq{}\bigoht(d^{2.5}\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Rewards concave = losses convex; mapped to function_class convex. DEC bound is from Lattimore (2020).

tuning: inverse gap weighting over eps-cover with eps = gamma^{-1/(d+1)}

source.label: prop:bandit_upper_lipschitz
source.quote: Since $\ActComp\leq\bigoht(d)$ for this setting, if we apply \pref{thm:upper_main_bayes} with this result we obtain $\En\brk{\RegDM} \leq \bigoht(T^{\frac{d+1}{d+2}})$ which matches the minimax rate derived in \cite{kleinberg2019bandits}.

results.notes: Text consequence; recovers known rate.

source.label: prop:bandit_lower_lipschitz
source.quote: Plugging this guarantee into \pref{thm:lower_main_expectation}, we obtain a lower bound of the form $\En\brk*{\RegDM}\geq\bigomt(T^{\frac{d+1}{d+2}})$, which again recovers the minimax rate.

results.notes: DEC bound: dec >= 2^-7 gamma^{-1/(d+1)}.

source.label: prop:bandit_lower_relu
source.quote: By plugging this result into \pref{thm:lower_main} and setting $\gamma=T$, we conclude that any algorithm must have $\RegDM \geq \bigom(\min\crl{e^{\Omega(d)},T})$ with constant probability, which further implies that $\En\brk*{\RegDM} \geq \bigom(\min\crl{e^{\Omega(d)},T})$.

results.notes: Recovers Dong et al. 2021 / Li et al. 2021.

source.label: eq:mab_gap
source.quote: Since minimax regret is non-decreasing with $T$, this implies a lower bound of the form $\En\brk*{\RegDM} \geq \bigom\prn*{\min\crl*{\Delta{}T, \frac{A}{\Delta}}}.$

results.notes: Minimax over the class of instances with gap Delta (not per-instance). Gap Delta is the best-vs-second-best gap, mapped to Delta_min.

source.label: eq:linear_gap
source.quote: Using similar calculations to the multi-armed bandit example, we deduce that any algorithm must have $\En\brk*{\RegDM} \geq \bigom\prn*{\min\crl*{\Delta{}T, \frac{d}{\Delta}}}.$

results.notes: Minimax over a constructed class with gap Delta.

conditions: d_E = sup_f eluder dimension of F_M - f at scale 1/T

source.label: thm:eluder_star
source.quote: this result recovers the $\bigoht(\sqrt{\ElDim{}T})$ regret bound derived in \cite{russo2013eluder} as a special case by appealing to \pref{thm:upper_main_bayes}

results.notes: Text consequence; estimation complexity term of thm:upper_main_bayes hidden in O_tilde.

source.label: thm:eluder_star
source.quote: but also implies a regret bound of the form $\bigoht(\sqrt{\StarDim^2{}T})$, which can be arbitrarily tighter.

results.notes: Text consequence of DEC bound in thm:eluder_star with thm:upper_main_bayes.

conditions: tabular MDP, sum of rewards in [0,1]

source.label: prop:igw_tabular
source.quote: Combining this with the \pcigw strategy (\pref{prop:igw_tabular}) and \mainalg (\pref{thm:upper_general}), we obtain an efficient algorithm with $\RegDM \leq \bigoht(\sqrt{H^{4}S^{3}A^2T})$.

results.notes: Probability type not explicit; out of scope (RL).

source.label: prop:lower_tabular
source.quote: we have that $\En\brk*{\RegDM} \geq{} \Omega(\sqrt{HSAT}).$

results.notes: Out of scope (RL).

symbols.est_Q: estimation complexity of the Q-function class inf_eps {log N(Q_M,eps) + eps^2 T}

source.label: thm:bilinear_refined
source.quote: This algorithm guarantees that for any prior $\mu\in\Delta(\cM)$ and $\gamma>0$, $\En_{\Mstar\sim\mu}\En\sups{\Mstar}\brk*{\RegDM} \leq{} \bigoht\prn*{\sqrt{H^2\Lbifulls\cdot{}\dimbifulls{}\cdot{}T\cdot{}\Qcomp}}.$ Consequently, we have $\MinimaxReg\leq ...$

results.notes: Also implies same minimax (frequentist) regret bound. Out of scope (RL).

source.label: prop:linear_qstar
source.quote: Using \pref{thm:lower_main} with $\gamma\propto{}T\log(T)$, we conclude that any algorithm for the linearly realizable setting must have $\RegDM \geq{} \bigomt\prn*{\min\crl*{2^{H}, 2^{\bigom(d)}, T}}$ with constant probability, which in turn implies that $\En\brk*{\RegDM} \geq{} ...$

results.notes: Out of scope (RL).

conditions: linearly realizable MDPs with H=1, deterministic rewards and dynamics, constant suboptimality gap

source.label: prop:mdp_gap_linear
source.quote: this result implies that any algorithm for the linearly realizable setting with deterministic dynamics and rewards must have $\RegDM \geq{} \bigomt\prn*{\min\crl*{d, T}}$ with constant probability, which in turn implies that $\En\brk*{\RegDM} \geq \bigomt\prn*{\min\crl*{d, T}}$.

results.notes: Recorded under RL setting (out of scope) although H=1.
